step1_revision_published.verification: Independent GET after PATCH: description starts '# OKR Weekly Standup — Revision 3'; old revision-2 placeholders {N} and {date range} absent.
step1_revision_published.note: PATCH /api/routines/{id} accepted `description` and bumped the revision, even though the published OpenAPI schema for that endpoint does not list `description` among its properties. Spec is incomplete; behaviour verified empirically.
step1_revision_published.descriptionDocumentFieldSkipped: patch-payload.json also carried a `descriptionDocument` object. It is not a field the routine GET returns and is not in the PATCH schema, so it was omitted. Its `body` was byte-identical to `description`, so no content was lost.

step2_dry_run.finding: The dispatcher created a NEW execution run (a0d3ad59) of the assignee and checked NFM-2050 out to it. This is the per-agent wake mechanism working at the platform level: routine fire -> issue created -> issue checked out to a fresh run of the assignee -> that run wakes with the issue as its payload.

step3_template_fill.result: FAIL — engine does not substitute placeholders
step3_template_fill.expectation: NFM-2049 step 4 expected the dry run to 'produce a filled template (not the raw {N} / {date range} placeholders)'.
step3_template_fill.actual: The engine copies routine.description into issue.description byte-for-byte. Generated issue description is 6031 chars, identical to the routine description.
step3_template_fill.titleNotFilled: The routine's `title` field is static text; the engine did not inject week/date into it either.
step3_template_fill.interpretation: Revision 3 removed the *revision-2* placeholders ({N}, {date range}) but introduced its own ({iso_week}, {mon}, {sun}, ...). Filling them is a PROCEDURAL step that revision 3 assigns to the assignee's execution run (description steps 1-3), not an engine feature. Therefore the NFM-2034 acceptance criterion 'routine revision published that fills week/date/roster automatically' is NOT met in the automatic sense — it is assignee-executed, which is the same fragility class as original defect #2.
step3_template_fill.canItBeAutomated: Undetermined. The routine model does expose a `variables` array ({name,label,type,defaultValue,required,options}) and POST /run accepts a `variables` object, so an interpolation feature plausibly exists. But no substitution syntax is documented anywhere in the OpenAPI spec, all 8 routines in this company have `variables: []`, and bare {x} demonstrably does NOT interpolate. The platform does use Handlebars-style {{...}} elsewhere (project workspaceStrategy.branchTemplate = '{{issue.identifier}}-{{slug}}'), which is the most promising lead. Escalated as a follow-up.

step4_fanout.reason: NFM-2050 is checked out to execution run a0d3ad59, not to this run (87f031bd). PATCH /api/issues/f1b08410... returned HTTP 409 with checkoutRunId=a0d3ad59 vs actorRunId=87f031bd. The fill and the 16-child fan-out are that run's work, driven by revision 3's 7-step instructions.
step4_fanout.whatIsProven: The wake path (routine -> issue -> fresh assignee run) is confirmed. The child-issue creation loop itself is unexecuted.
step4_fanout.deliberateScopeDecision: Even with write access, a full 16-reporter fan-out was NOT the right action here. NFM-2050 is an ISO week 31 issue created Thursday 2026-07-30 01:50 Asia/Shanghai; week 31's window (Mon 09:30 -> Fri 17:00) had ~1.6 days left. Fanning out 16 reporters into a near-closed window would produce an artificially poor first cycle and burn 16 agent runs on a validation artifact, three days before the real Monday 2026-08-03 (ISO week 32) cycle. First full production cycle is deliberately week 32.

step5_roster_validation.verification: Every one of the 16 reporter UUIDs in revision 3 resolves to a live agent and the names match the spec. 16 reporters + 7 excluded = 23 = full live roster, so the partition is exhaustive with no agent unaccounted for.

step6_iso_week_check.claim: NFM-1909 labelled 2026-07-20 -> 2026-07-26 as 'Week 31'; correct ISO label is Week 30.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Routine revision published that fills week/date/roster automatically
acceptanceCriteria.detail: Revision 3 published and live. 'Automatically' is not satisfied: the engine does verbatim copy; fill is assignee-executed. See step3.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Documented, implemented fan-out path proven on at least one dry run
acceptanceCriteria.detail: Documented in revision 3 and spec.md. Dispatch/wake half proven by this dry run. Child-issue creation loop not yet executed — belongs to run a0d3ad59 / the week-32 cycle.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Written definition of responder set, window, and close-out owner
acceptanceCriteria.detail: Revision 3 defines all three, and the responder set is now validated against the live roster.
Cannot be observed until a cycle runs its fan-out. Target: Monday 2026-08-03 (ISO week 32).

residualRisk: The single point of failure is unchanged in kind: if the assignee's execution run does not perform steps 1-4 of revision 3, the cycle again emits a raw-placeholder issue with no fan-out. Revision 3 makes the procedure explicit and auditable, but does not make it mechanical.
